obtained.how: the report PDF from ASMFC's own website (the ledger URL)

bibliography.checked_against: the cover (PDF p. 1: 'River Herring Benchmark Stock Assessment and Peer Review Report — Accepted for Management Use by the Shad and River Herring Management Board, August 7, 2024')
bibliography.note: 499 PDF pages: Section A peer review (PDF pp. 4–24), Section B assessment (PDF pp. 25–499, its own page numbers), Section C appendices. Section B page numbers are used below.

claims.claim: northern New England females L∞ 300 mm, K 0.66 (ASMFC 2024)
claims.conditions: sex-specific von Bertalanffy fits, NNE alewife stock-region (St. Croix River to the Merrimack River), ages from otoliths; L∞ is mean asymptotic total length in mm; posterior means with 95 % credible intervals; t0 −0.39
claims.note: Total length and otolith ages, as the notes say. Scale-based ages give lower values (female K 0.68, L∞ 291.78 mm); males (otolith) K 0.70, L∞ 286.55 mm. Individual NNE rivers ranged from L∞ 275 to 345 mm for females (p. 96).

claims.source_value: an assumption of the maturity model, not a finding: 'All fish were assumed immature below age 3 and mature by age 6' (Maki et al. 2001 method on scale spawning marks), chosen because in first-time-spawner (virgin) collections 'Few age 2 examples were observed', ages 3–5 were common and age-6 virgins 'generally rare'; the proportion mature at ages 3–5 was then estimated by region and sex. The report's background says 'Most river herring reach sexual maturity between 3 and 6 years of age' (p. 13)
claims.location: Section B p. 80 (PDF p. 124), §4.1.2 Maturity Curves; Section A p. 12 (peer review summary); Section B p. 13 (PDF p. 57)
claims.quote: All fish were assumed immature below age 3 and mature by age 6
claims.conditions: coastwide method, applied per stock-region and sex; immature fish are scarce in the in-river samples
claims.note: The digits match but the conditions do not: it is a modelling cut-off (with a few age-2 first spawners observed), so the table should say 'maturity mostly at 3–5 (ASMFC 2024; the assessment assumes none before 3 and all by 6)' or use the background sentence 'most mature at 3–6'. The peer-review section (Section A p. 12) restates it as 'all fish younger than 3 were immature, and all fish older than 5 were mature'.

notes: Other NNE values that could serve the model: Z40%SPR median 0.96 (95 % CI 0.75–1.62) for NNE alewife (p. 96); maximum age in Maine commercial runs mostly 5–7, range 4–9 (p. 96). The report's background says alewives 'further north' typically spawn from June through August (p. 13) — a coastwide generalisation that sits later than the Maine run timing (early May–early June) the table takes from Kircheis et al. 2002; worth a look by whoever checks that entry.
